science_brief: Science brief: displacement is a vector from start point to end point; distance is the scalar path length travelled.
Science brief: position is stated relative to a chosen origin and reference frame, and the choice must be stated before positions mean anything.
Science brief: displacement depends only on start and end points; distance depends on the whole path, so the two differ whenever the path is not straight.
Science brief: motion described in one reference frame may be described quite differently in another, and neither description is wrong.

science_brief: Science brief: displacement is a vector from start point to end point; distance is the scalar path length travelled.
Science brief: position is stated relative to a chosen origin and reference frame, and the choice must be stated before positions mean anything.
Science brief: displacement depends only on start and end points; distance depends on the whole path, so the two differ whenever the path is not straight.
Science brief: motion described in one reference frame may be described quite differently in another, and neither description is wrong.

disqualifying_errors: Reporting displacement as equal to distance for a path that is not straight and one-directional.
Describing a position or a motion with no reference frame or origin stated.
Claiming displacement can exceed the distance travelled.
fixed_facts: Displacement is a vector from start point to end point; distance is the scalar path length travelled.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Relativistic reference frames and non-inertial frame corrections are beyond this course.
relationships: Position is stated relative to a chosen origin and reference frame, and the choice must be stated before positions mean anything.
Displacement depends only on start and end points; distance depends on the whole path, so the two differ whenever the path is not straight.
Motion described in one reference frame may be described quite differently in another, and neither description is wrong.

science_brief: Science brief: velocity is the rate of change of position; acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Science brief: acceleration is non-zero whenever speed changes, direction changes, or both.
Science brief: velocity is a vector: it has magnitude and direction, and speed is its magnitude.
Science brief: an object moving at constant speed around a curve is accelerating, because its direction, and therefore its velocity, is changing.

SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear the run and the floor beyond it, and set a soft barrier at the end before the first release.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Set the raised end no higher than 30 cm, tape the start line, and keep pets and young children out of the area.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Release from the same marked point every trial and record each timing immediately.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Retrieve the rolling object only after it has stopped.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the ball repeatedly leaves the intended path.
  STOP: Stop if anyone enters the run area.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.

  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.

ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Analyse a published motion dataset or a frame-numbered motion diagram supplied on paper, extracting velocity and acceleration by hand. No ramp, no timing, paper only.

disqualifying_errors: Reading a position-time graph as a map of the object's path.
Claiming the slope of a velocity-time graph gives velocity, or that its area gives acceleration.
Claiming a horizontal line on a position-time graph shows motion at a constant non-zero speed rather than rest.
fixed_facts: On a position-time graph the slope is velocity; on a velocity-time graph the slope is acceleration and the area under the curve is displacement.

relationships: The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity, including its sign, which carries direction.
The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration, and the area between the curve and the time axis gives displacement.
A graph represents the motion; it is not a picture of the path the object took through space.

science_brief: Science brief: a free-body diagram shows only the forces acting on the chosen object, not the forces that object exerts on others.
Science brief: each force on the diagram has an identified source: another object that is in contact with, or interacting at a distance with, the chosen body.
Science brief: the two forces of an interaction pair act on different objects and therefore never appear on the same free-body diagram.
Science brief: motion itself is not a force, so no arrow is drawn for the object's own movement.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Falling weights can land on feet or break flooring.
MITIGATION: Keep the hanging mass under 200 g, place a cushion or towel below the drop zone, keep feet clear, and never stand under the hanging mass.
HAZARD (physical): String under tension can snap back toward the face.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection whenever the string is under tension, use light loads only, inspect the string along its whole length before each run, and stand to the side of the string line rather than in it.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Put a cushion or folded towel under the drop zone and keep every foot clear of it.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection before the string is put under any tension.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Inspect the string along its whole length before each run and replace it at the first sign of fraying.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Start with the lightest load and add mass, up to 200 g, only after a clean run.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Stand to the side of the string line, never in it, and never under the hanging mass.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the string frays or the pulley slips.
  STOP: Stop if anyone's feet are in the drop zone.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Coil the string and put the weights back into a container out of reach of young children. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use a published force-mass-acceleration dataset and a supplied set of free-body diagrams; derive the relationship graphically. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.

  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.

  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Applying the relationship to one individual force rather than the net force.
Claiming acceleration is in the direction of motion rather than of net force.
Claiming force is proportional to velocity rather than to acceleration.
fixed_facts: Acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass, and it is in the direction of the net force.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Variable-mass systems and the momentum form of the second law are acceptable but not required.
relationships: For a given mass, doubling the net force doubles the acceleration; for a given net force, doubling the mass halves it.
The relationship applies to the net force, not to any single force acting on the object.
Acceleration is always in the direction of the net force, whatever the direction of motion.

science_brief: Science brief: mass is a property of the object and does not change with location; weight is the gravitational force on it and does.
Science brief: mass measures how strongly an object resists a change in motion and is measured in kilograms.
Science brief: weight is a force, measured in newtons, equal to mass times the local gravitational field strength.
Science brief: an object in free fall or in orbit still has weight; what it lacks is a supporting normal force, which is why it feels weightless.

science_brief: Science brief: impulse is force multiplied by the time it acts, and it equals the change in momentum.
Science brief: for a given change in momentum, extending the contact time reduces the average force.
Science brief: this is why crumple zones, airbags, helmets, and catching techniques reduce peak force, without reducing the momentum change.
Science brief: impulse is a vector in the direction of the average force.

science_brief: Science brief: momentum is conserved in all collisions; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones.
Science brief: in an elastic collision total kinetic energy is unchanged; in an inelastic collision some is transferred to deformation, sound, and thermal energy.
Science brief: in a perfectly inelastic collision the objects move off together, and kinetic energy loss is at its maximum for that momentum.
Science brief: real macroscopic collisions are never perfectly elastic, though some are close enough to model that way.

fixed_facts: Momentum is conserved in all collisions; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones.

relationships: In an elastic collision total kinetic energy is unchanged; in an inelastic collision some is transferred to deformation, sound, and thermal energy.

science_brief: Science brief: momentum is mass times velocity, and it is a vector with the same direction as the velocity.
Science brief: momentum depends on both mass and velocity, so a slow heavy object and a fast light one can carry the same momentum.
Science brief: momentum is a vector, so its direction matters and momenta in opposite directions partly cancel.
Science brief: momentum and kinetic energy are different quantities and are not interchangeable.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Dropping objects from height risks falls and impacts.
MITIGATION: Drop from standing height at most, never from a ladder, chair, or window. The learner stands clear of the landing zone.
HAZARD (physical): Raw egg is a salmonella exposure and a slip hazard.
MITIGATION: Contain every drop in a tray or tarp, wear gloves whenever anyone has a cut or graze, wash hands thoroughly after every trial without exception, disinfect the area, and never eat or drink in the work area.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Line the landing zone with the tray or tarp before any egg leaves its box.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on gloves if anyone has a cut or graze, and drop from standing height only - never from a chair, ladder, step, or window.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Keep everyone clear of the landing zone for every drop.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Clean and disinfect after every broken egg before the next trial begins.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Wash hands thoroughly after every trial, and never eat or drink in the work area.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if anyone climbs on furniture to increase drop height.
  STOP: Stop and clean thoroughly if raw egg contacts skin, and wash hands before touching anything else.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Broken egg, shell, and any padding that touched raw egg go straight into a bin liner and into the bin - contaminated padding is never reused and never laundered with household washing. Wash the tray, tarp, and surfaces with hot soapy water and disinfect them. Bin the gloves and wash hands thoroughly before any food is handled.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use a sealed water balloon, a small beanbag, or a marshmallow instead of an egg - no biological hazard, no cleanup - or run the collision strand with toy cars only and analyse published crash-test data for the protective design. Both paths meet the same momentum and impulse target.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a protective device reduces the change in momentum rather than the peak force.
Claiming impulse and force are the same quantity.
Claiming a longer contact time increases the force for the same momentum change.
fixed_facts: Impulse is force multiplied by the time it acts, and it equals the change in momentum.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Force-time curve integration for non-constant forces is acceptable but not required.
relationships: For a given change in momentum, extending the contact time reduces the average force.
This is why crumple zones, airbags, helmets, and catching techniques reduce peak force, without reducing the momentum change.
Impulse is a vector in the direction of the average force.

science_brief: Science brief: momentum is conserved in all collisions; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones.
Science brief: in an elastic collision total kinetic energy is unchanged; in an inelastic collision some is transferred to deformation, sound, and thermal energy.
Science brief: in a perfectly inelastic collision the objects move off together, and kinetic energy loss is at its maximum for that momentum.
Science brief: real macroscopic collisions are never perfectly elastic, though some are close enough to model that way.

Claiming momentum is not conserved in an inelastic collision.

fixed_facts: Momentum is conserved in all collisions; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones.

relationships: In an elastic collision total kinetic energy is unchanged; in an inelastic collision some is transferred to deformation, sound, and thermal energy.

Real macroscopic collisions are never perfectly elastic, though some are close enough to model that way.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Balloons can pop suddenly and are a choking hazard for young children.
MITIGATION: No balloon is inflated where a child under four is present. Keep whole balloons and every fragment away from young children, and anyone with a latex allergy uses the light-intensity route instead.
HAZARD (physical): Static discharge is startling though harmless at this scale, but a spark near fuel vapour is not.
MITIGATION: Keep all static work away from electronics, and never perform it near a computer, a gas hob, a petrol can, a fuel-storage shed, an aerosol, or any flammable liquid.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Ask about latex allergy before a balloon is opened, and check no child under four is present. If either applies, run the light-intensity route instead.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Move phones, laptops, cards, and every electronic device off the work surface before any static work.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Check that no gas hob, petrol can, aerosol, or flammable liquid is anywhere near the work area.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Charge and test one balloon at a time, keeping fragments off the floor.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop static work near any electronic device.
  STOP: Switch to the light route if anyone present has a latex allergy.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Deflate the balloons and put whole balloons and every fragment straight into the bin - fragments are a choking hazard for young children. Recycle the paper pieces. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Measure illuminated area against distance with a flashlight and a ruler and work the relationship out from your own measurements; no relationship and no expected value is supplied in advance. Then apply the same mathematics to gravitation and Coulomb's law using published masses and charges. Household items and paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

science_brief: Science brief: kinetic energy depends on mass and on the square of the speed; gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height above a chosen reference.
Science brief: doubling an object's speed quadruples its kinetic energy, which is why stopping distance grows so steeply with speed.
Science brief: potential energy is defined relative to a chosen reference level, and only differences in it are physically meaningful.
Science brief: potential energy belongs to a system of interacting objects, such as an object and Earth, not to one object alone.

science_brief: Science brief: an energy budget lists the energy in the system at the start, the transfers in and out, and the energy at the end, and the two sides must agree within uncertainty.
Science brief: a shortfall in the budget points to an unaccounted transfer, most often dissipation, and it is identified rather than absorbed into a residual.
Science brief: every term in the budget carries the uncertainty of the measurements it came from.

science_brief: Science brief: kinetic energy depends on mass and on the square of the speed; gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height above a chosen reference.
Science brief: doubling an object's speed quadruples its kinetic energy, which is why stopping distance grows so steeply with speed.
Science brief: potential energy is defined relative to a chosen reference level, and only differences in it are physically meaningful.
Science brief: potential energy belongs to a system of interacting objects, such as an object and Earth, not to one object alone.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): A swinging pendulum or bouncing ball can strike a person or object.
MITIGATION: Clear a radius larger than the string length, keep the bob under 200 g, swing at small angles, and keep faces and screens out of the swing plane.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear a radius larger than the string length and move screens, faces, and breakables out of the swing plane.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Check the string for fraying before each set of trials.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Keep the bob under 200 g and release from small angles only.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Record each trial before changing anything, and stop the bob by hand only once it has slowed.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the bob or ball leaves the cleared area.
  STOP: Stop if the string shows any sign of fraying.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Untie and coil the string and put the ball or bob away. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Build the energy budget from a supplied table of published bounce heights or pendulum periods, computing the model by hand. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

fixed_facts: Kinetic energy depends on mass and on the square of the speed; gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height above a chosen reference.

science_brief: Science brief: energy is conserved: the total energy of a closed system is constant, and energy transfers or transforms rather than being created or destroyed.
Science brief: an energy account requires a defined system and boundary, since what counts as a transfer depends on where the boundary lies.
Science brief: energy changes form within the system and is transferred across the boundary by work, by heating, or by radiation.
Science brief: an account that does not balance indicates an unidentified transfer, not a failure of conservation.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): A swinging pendulum or bouncing ball can strike a person or object.
MITIGATION: Clear a radius larger than the string length, keep the bob under 200 g, swing at small angles, and keep faces and screens out of the swing plane.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear a radius larger than the string length and move screens, faces, and breakables out of the swing plane.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Check the string for fraying before each set of trials.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Keep the bob under 200 g and release from small angles only.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Record each trial before changing anything, and stop the bob by hand only once it has slowed.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the bob or ball leaves the cleared area.
  STOP: Stop if the string shows any sign of fraying.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Untie and coil the string and put the ball or bob away. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Build the energy budget from a supplied table of published bounce heights or pendulum periods, computing the model by hand. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

science_brief: Science brief: the thermal energy of an object is the energy associated with the random motion of its particles.
Science brief: macroscopic kinetic energy is associated with the ordered motion of an object as a whole; thermal energy is associated with the random motion of its particles.
Science brief: friction and inelastic collisions convert ordered macroscopic energy into random particle energy, which is why they raise temperature.
Science brief: energy is conserved across the two scales, so an apparent macroscopic loss appears as a particle-scale gain.

fixed_facts: The thermal energy of an object is the energy associated with the random motion of its particles.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Statistical mechanics and equipartition are beyond this course.
relationships: Macroscopic kinetic energy is associated with the ordered motion of an object as a whole; thermal energy is associated with the random motion of its particles.
Friction and inelastic collisions convert ordered macroscopic energy into random particle energy, which is why they raise temperature.
Energy is conserved across the two scales, so an apparent macroscopic loss appears as a particle-scale gain.

Science brief: two objects at the same temperature can hold very different amounts of thermal energy, because thermal energy depends on mass and material as well.

Science brief: temperature determines the direction of spontaneous thermal transfer; total thermal energy does not.

Science brief: two objects at the same temperature can hold very different amounts of thermal energy, because thermal energy depends on mass and material as well.
Science brief: adding thermal energy to a substance raises its temperature, except during a change of state, when it changes particle arrangement instead.
Science brief: temperature determines the direction of spontaneous thermal transfer; total thermal energy does not.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Hot water scalds, and the risk rises with temperature.
MITIGATION: Keep all water below 50 degrees Celsius. An adult measures and pours every warm sample. The learner never carries an open container of warm water.
HAZARD (physical): Thermometers can break; mercury thermometers must never be used.
MITIGATION: Use a digital or alcohol thermometer only. If any thermometer breaks, an adult clears it.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult measures and pours every warm sample and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 50 degrees Celsius; the learner never carries an open container of warm water.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Use a digital or alcohol thermometer only. A mercury thermometer is never used for any part of this unit.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Record the starting temperature of each component before they are combined.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Combine, close the insulated cup, and read at fixed intervals rather than opening it repeatedly.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Let everything cool before it is emptied.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if water exceeds 50 degrees Celsius.
  STOP: Stop and let an adult clear any broken thermometer.
  STOP: Never use a mercury thermometer for any part of this unit.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the cooled water down the drain, dry the cups and thermos, and put the thermometer away in its case. If any thermometer breaks, an adult clears it: pieces are lifted with stiff card into a rigid container and binned separately, never with bare hands and never with a vacuum cleaner.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use a published cooling-curve dataset, or run the whole investigation at room temperature versus refrigerator temperature - no heating at all. Both meet the equilibration target.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.

disqualifying_errors: Treating temperature and thermal energy as the same quantity.
Claiming the object with more thermal energy is necessarily at the higher temperature.
Claiming temperature rises steadily while a substance is melting or boiling.
fixed_facts: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles; thermal energy is the total energy of that random motion and also depends on how much material there is.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Absolute temperature scales beyond conversion, and kinetic theory derivations, are beyond this course.
relationships: Two objects at the same temperature can hold very different amounts of thermal energy, because thermal energy depends on mass and material as well.
Adding thermal energy to a substance raises its temperature, except during a change of state, when it changes particle arrangement instead.
Temperature determines the direction of spontaneous thermal transfer; total thermal energy does not.

science_brief: Science brief: conduction transfers energy through particle interaction, convection through bulk fluid movement, and radiation by electromagnetic waves requiring no medium.
Science brief: conduction requires matter in contact and is fastest in materials with mobile electrons, which is why metals conduct thermally as well as electrically.
Science brief: convection requires a fluid free to move, so it does not occur within a solid.
Science brief: radiation occurs across a vacuum and is how energy reaches Earth from the Sun.

Confusing specific heat capacity with thermal conductivity.
Applying the specific heat relationship across a change of state.
fixed_facts: Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one kelvin, and it differs between substances.

relationships: For the same energy input and the same mass, a substance with higher specific heat capacity shows a smaller temperature rise.
Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity, which is why large bodies of water moderate nearby climates.
The energy transferred is the product of mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change.

science_brief: Science brief: thermal energy does not flow spontaneously from a cooler body to a warmer one, and no cyclic device converts thermal energy entirely into work.
Science brief: energy spontaneously disperses, so the total disorder of a system and its surroundings does not decrease.
Science brief: a refrigerator or heat pump moves energy from cooler to warmer only because work is supplied, so the overall dispersal still increases.
Science brief: this sets an upper limit on the efficiency of any heat engine that is strictly below one hundred per cent.

hazards.description: Swallowed magnets are a surgical emergency: two or more magnets, or a magnet and any swallowed metal object, attract through the wall of the gut and cut off its blood supply.

hazards.description: A wire connected across a battery heats rapidly and can burn skin or start a fire, and a nail is a magnetic core rather than a resistance.
hazards.mitigation: Use at least 1 m of thin 28-30 AWG enamelled wire so the coil has real resistance; a short or thick wire is a short circuit even with a nail through it. One 1.5 V cell only - NEVER mains, lithium, or button cell.

hazards.description: A multimeter left on a current range and placed across a battery ruptures its fuse and can arc.
hazards.mitigation: The multimeter stays on a voltage range for every measurement in this investigation. A current range is never placed across a cell.

hazards.description: Strong neodymium magnets pinch skin severely and destroy electronics and cards.
hazards.mitigation: Handle magnets one at a time, keep them well away from phones, laptops, bank cards, and any medical device such as a pacemaker, and store them separated.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Swallowed magnets are a surgical emergency: two or more magnets, or a magnet and any swallowed metal object, attract through the wall of the gut and cut off its blood supply.
MITIGATION: Count the magnets out and back in every session, work over a tray, never bring one near a mouth, and store them closed and labelled out of reach of children and pets. A suspected swallow is an emergency: go at once.
HAZARD (physical): A wire connected across a battery heats rapidly and can burn skin or start a fire, and a nail is a magnetic core rather than a resistance.
MITIGATION: Use at least 1 m of thin 28-30 AWG enamelled wire so the coil has real resistance; a short or thick wire is a short circuit even with a nail through it. One 1.5 V cell only - NEVER mains, lithium, or button cell.
HAZARD (physical): A multimeter left on a current range and placed across a battery ruptures its fuse and can arc.
MITIGATION: The multimeter stays on a voltage range for every measurement in this investigation. A current range is never placed across a cell.
HAZARD (physical): Strong neodymium magnets pinch skin severely and destroy electronics and cards.
MITIGATION: Handle magnets one at a time, keep them well away from phones, laptops, bank cards, and any medical device such as a pacemaker, and store them separated.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Count the magnets and record the total before anything else, and keep them on a tray so none can reach the floor.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Move phones, laptops, and bank cards well away, and keep anyone with an implanted medical device out of the work area.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Build the coil with at least 1 m of thin enamelled wire so it has real resistance; the nail is a core, not a resistance.
  SAFE ORDER 4. An adult makes every connection, with the coil always in the circuit, for a few seconds at a time, disconnecting between trials.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep the multimeter on a voltage range throughout; a current range is never placed across a cell.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Count every magnet back into its closed labelled box and disconnect the cell before anyone leaves the work area.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and account for every magnet before anyone leaves the work area.
  STOP: Stop immediately and disconnect if the wire, battery, or nail becomes warm.
  STOP: Stop if a magnet approaches any electronic device, anyone with an implanted medical device, or anyone's mouth.
  STOP: Never connect any part of this investigation to a wall outlet.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Disconnect and remove the cell, tape its terminals, and store used cells in a labelled container for household battery recycling - never loose in a drawer, never in the general bin, and never near steel wool. Magnets go back into a closed labelled box, counted, out of reach of children and pets. Wire and nail are put away. No lithium or button cell is used anywhere in this investigation.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Map a magnetic field with a compass and a permanent magnet only - no battery, no circuit - and study induction from published data or a supplied diagram sequence. Compass and paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.

  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.

  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a magnetic field exerts a force on a stationary charge.
Claiming isolated magnetic north or south poles can be produced by cutting a magnet.
Treating field lines as physical objects rather than a representation.
fixed_facts: Electric fields exert forces on charges whether or not they are moving; magnetic fields exert forces only on moving charges and on magnetic materials.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Maxwell's equations, field energy density, and relativistic field transformation are beyond this course.
relationships: A field is a model in which one object modifies the space around it, and a second object responds to the field at its own location.
The electric field direction is defined as the direction of the force on a positive test charge.
Magnetic field lines form closed loops; isolated magnetic poles have never been observed.

science_brief: Science brief: an electric current produces a magnetic field around it.

Science brief: a current-carrying conductor in an external magnetic field experiences a force, which is the basis of the electric motor.

science_brief: Science brief: a voltage is induced in a circuit only when the magnetic flux through it is changing.
Science brief: relative motion between a conductor and a magnetic field, or a changing field strength, changes the flux and induces a voltage.
Science brief: a steady magnetic field with no relative motion induces nothing, however strong it is.
Science brief: the induced effect opposes the change that produced it, which is why generators require work to turn.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming one of the two models has been shown to be the correct one and the other abandoned.
Claiming photon energy depends on the brightness of the light rather than on its frequency.
Claiming light requires a medium to travel through.
fixed_facts: Light shows wave behaviour such as diffraction and interference, and particle behaviour such as the photoelectric effect; neither model alone accounts for all observations.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Quantum mechanics, the photoelectric equation, and de Broglie wavelength are acceptable to reference but not required.
relationships: The wave model explains interference, diffraction, and refraction; the particle model explains the photoelectric effect and the discreteness of light emission and absorption.
Which model applies depends on the experiment; the two are not competing claims about which is really true.
Photon energy increases with frequency, which is why the effect of light on matter depends on frequency rather than on brightness alone.

science_brief: Science brief: a wave transfers energy without net transport of the medium.

Science brief: frequency and period are reciprocals of one another.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): A stretched spring released under tension snaps back hard and can injure eyes.
MITIGATION: Everyone wears eye protection whenever the spring is under tension. Two people hold the ends, never stretch beyond about twice the resting length, never let go while stretched, and release slowly together.
HAZARD (physical): Bright light sources can damage vision.
MITIGATION: Use a flashlight or LED only. NO LASER of any kind is used in this unit. Never look directly into any light source or point one at another person.
HAZARD (physical): A snapped or scored CD throws sharp shards.
MITIGATION: Use an intact CD or a sheet diffraction grating. Never cut, score, or snap a disc.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Everyone in the room puts on eye protection before the spring is stretched at all.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Two people take the ends and everyone else stands clear of the line of the spring.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Stretch to no more than about twice the resting length and never let go while it is stretched.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Run the pulse timings, then release the tension slowly and deliberately together.
  SAFE ORDER 5. For the light strand use a flashlight or LED only, pointed at the tray or the intact CD and never toward a face. No laser is used, and no disc is cut, scored, or snapped.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the spring is stretched near its limit or if anyone is in its recoil path.
  STOP: Stop if any light source is pointed toward a face.
  STOP: Do not substitute a laser pointer for the flashlight under any circumstances.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Coil the spring or rope loosely and put it away, empty the water tray down the drain and dry it, and return the CD or grating to its sleeve. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Measure wave speed on a rope on the floor - no tension, no recoil - and observe diffraction with a CD held under a household lamp. Or work from published wave-speed tables and a supplied refraction diagram. No spring, no bright source.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a wave carries the medium along with it.
Confusing amplitude with wavelength, or frequency with wave speed.
Claiming sound is a transverse wave in air.
fixed_facts: A wave transfers energy without net transport of the medium.
Amplitude is maximum displacement from equilibrium; wavelength is the distance between matching points on successive cycles; frequency is cycles per second; period is the time for one cycle.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Wave equation derivation and polarisation are acceptable but not required.
relationships: Particles of a medium oscillate about fixed positions while the wave and its energy travel through.
Frequency and period are reciprocals of one another.
In a transverse wave the oscillation is perpendicular to the direction of travel; in a longitudinal wave it is along it.

fixed_facts: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.

relationships: In a given medium the wave speed is fixed by the medium, so frequency and wavelength vary inversely with each other.

The relationship holds for all waves, mechanical and electromagnetic alike.

science_brief: Science brief: reflection returns a wave from a boundary, refraction is the change of direction on entering a medium where the speed differs, and diffraction is the spreading of a wave past an edge or through a gap.
Science brief: in reflection from a smooth surface the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the normal.
Science brief: refraction occurs because the wave speed changes at the boundary; a wave entering along the normal changes speed without changing direction.
Science brief: diffraction is most pronounced when the gap or obstacle is comparable in size to the wavelength.

science_brief: Science brief: whether radiation is absorbed, transmitted, or reflected depends on both the material and the frequency of the radiation.
Science brief: absorption transfers energy from the radiation to the material, commonly raising its temperature or exciting its electrons.
Science brief: a material transparent to one part of the spectrum can be opaque to another, which is why glass passes visible light but blocks much ultraviolet.
Science brief: ionising radiation damages matter by removing electrons from atoms, which non-ionising radiation cannot do however intense it is.

science_brief: Science brief: digital signals encode information in discrete values; analog signals vary continuously.
Science brief: noise added to an analog signal becomes part of it, while a digital signal can be restored by rounding each value to the nearest allowed level.
Science brief: that restorability is why digital signals survive repeated transmission and copying far better than analog ones.
Science brief: digitising a continuous signal involves sampling and rounding, so it loses some information; how much depends on the sampling and the levels used.

disqualifying_errors: Treating all radiation as equivalent in its effects on matter or on people.
Claiming a non-ionising source becomes ionising at high power.
Accepting or rejecting a published claim without reference to the evidence or the study design behind it.
fixed_facts: The distinction between ionising and non-ionising radiation is set by photon energy, which depends on frequency, not by the power of the source.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Epidemiological methods, exposure standards, and health physics are beyond this course.
relationships: Evaluating a claim about radiation means identifying which part of the spectrum is involved, at what intensity, and over what exposure.
A claim's strength depends on the study design and on whether independent work agrees, not on the confidence of the presentation.
The word radiation covers everything from radio waves to gamma rays, so a claim about radiation that does not specify which is not evaluable.

science_brief: Science brief: in order of increasing frequency and decreasing wavelength the spectrum runs radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma.
Science brief: all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum, approximately three times ten to the eighth metres per second.
Science brief: the regions of the spectrum differ in frequency and wavelength, not in their fundamental nature.
Science brief: photon energy increases with frequency, so gamma rays carry far more energy per photon than radio waves.

  SAFE ORDER 5. Run each test for a few seconds, disconnecting between tests, and disconnect at once if a motor stalls or anything warms.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Disconnect and remove the cell before the build is stored.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if any component becomes warm.
  STOP: Stop if a source requests an account, payment, or personal information.
  STOP: Never connect any build to a wall outlet.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.

science_brief: Science brief: whether radiation is absorbed, transmitted, or reflected depends on both the material and the frequency of the radiation.
Science brief: absorption transfers energy from the radiation to the material, commonly raising its temperature or exciting its electrons.
Science brief: a material transparent to one part of the spectrum can be opaque to another, which is why glass passes visible light but blocks much ultraviolet.
Science brief: ionising radiation damages matter by removing electrons from atoms, which non-ionising radiation cannot do however intense it is.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming digital signals are unaffected by noise or loss.
Claiming digitisation preserves the original signal exactly.
Claiming an analog signal can be cleaned of accumulated noise as a digital one can.
fixed_facts: Digital signals encode information in discrete values; analog signals vary continuously.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Sampling theorem, quantisation error analysis, and coding theory are beyond this course.
relationships: Noise added to an analog signal becomes part of it, while a digital signal can be restored by rounding each value to the nearest allowed level.
That restorability is why digital signals survive repeated transmission and copying far better than analog ones.
Digitising a continuous signal involves sampling and rounding, so it loses some information; how much depends on the sampling and the levels used.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a device produces more energy than it receives.
Reporting an efficiency without stating what was measured as input and as useful output.
Changing several design features at once and attributing the improvement to one.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Thermodynamic efficiency limits for specific cycles and formal design optimisation are beyond this course.
relationships: An energy conversion device is evaluated on measured input, measured useful output, and the difference between them.
No device converts all input to useful output, so an efficiency claim of one hundred per cent indicates a measurement or accounting error.
Design improvements are tested one change at a time against the stated criteria.
